definitions.phases_of_play: Each team's live-ball time split into six phases: attacking (settled possession), defending (settled out of possession), attacking and defensive transitions (the first 10 s after an open-play regain or loss, or 15 s while it is a counter that reached the final third) and set pieces (the first 10 s after a corner, free kick or throw-in, attacking or defending). Goal kicks and kick-offs start the attacking phase. Shots, xG and goals are credited to the phase in which the shot's possession was at the time.
definitions.counter: An attacking transition that reaches the final third (x ≥ 66.67) within 10 s of an open-play regain outside it. Recycled: the first action after the regain goes sideways or backward (less than 5 m of depth). Lost quickly: the possession ends within 5 s without reaching the final third. Counter shots are shots within 15 s of a regain.
definitions.counter_press: After each open-play loss, from the 5 Hz synthetic positions: pressed when a player other than the one who lost it gets within 3 m of the ball within 3 s; the pack is how many of the team's outfield players are within 10 m of the ball 2 s after the loss. Regained within 5 or 10 s comes from the events. Bypassed: the opponent moved the ball 20 m or more upfield within 10 s.
definitions.rest_defence: At the moment of each loss: how many outfield players were goal-side of the ball (nearer their own goal than it), and how many of those were back-four defenders.
definitions.blocks: Settled defending time (out of possession, outside transitions and set pieces) classed every 200 ms by the back four's mean depth: high at 42 m or more, low under 30 m, mid in between. For each block: length (deepest to highest outfield player), width, the gap between the back four and the midfield three, players in their own box while the ball is in their defending third (35 m), and what the opponent did against it.
definitions.wide_entries: Opponent entries into its final third (completed passes and carries) ending in a wide channel (y < 33.3 or y > 66.7): the share of entries a block forced wide.
definitions.long_shots: Shots from outside the penalty area.
definitions.crosses_faced: Opponent passes from a wide channel of its final third into the penalty area.
definitions.line_snapshots: The line during the opponent's first build-up (the first 8 s of a possession it starts in its own third from a restart or its goalkeeper) and during a high press (the opponent has the ball in its own third and one of the team's players is within 5 m of it), against settled defending. Front line: mean depth of the three forwards.
definitions.recovery: Balls in behind: opponent completed passes that end nearer the team's goal than its deepest outfield player, within 45 m of goal. Retreat is the back four's mean drop in depth over the next 5 s; top speed their fastest recovery speed; the keeper's distance from the goal line as the pass is played and the furthest within 5 s. A sweep is the keeper leaving the penalty area (16.5 m) in that time.
definitions.progressive_carry: A carry that moves the ball at least 10 m closer to the centre of the opponent's goal, or 5 m when it starts in the final 40% of the pitch (x ≥ 60), and ends further forward than it started (StatsBomb / FBref convention). Progressive carry metres add up the forward distance of those carries.
definitions.take_on: A carry that beat a challenge on the way (the defender lost the ground duel). Unlike a progressive carry it says nothing about how far the ball moved.
definitions.xt: Expected threat: each zone of a 12 x 8 grid has the chance that a possession there ends in a goal within the next few actions, learned by value iteration from how play moved in 24 other synthetic matches (never this one). A completed pass or carry is worth xT(end zone) − xT(start zone). Failed actions are not valued, as in the original method.
definitions.xt_vs_pv: Possession value (in Live analytics) uses a hand-set surface that rises steadily toward goal. xT is learned from the synthetic matches, so it shows where that play really leads to shots, including quirks of the generator.
definitions.fullback_style: From the 5 Hz synthetic positions while the team has the ball: inverted when the full-back spends 40% or more of build-up time 18 m or more from the touchline; overlapping or underlapping when it gets ahead of its winger outside (wider) or inside (narrower) at least 3 times and twice as often as the other way; holding when, with the ball in the final third, it stays under 52 m from its own goal on average; otherwise balanced. At least 60 s in possession is needed.
definitions.overlap: A full-back at least 2 m ahead of the winger on its side and at least 3 m wider, for 1 s or more. An underlap is the same run 3 m or more inside the winger.
definitions.rotations: Position swaps held for 2 s or more while the team has the ball: the holding midfielder dropping level with or behind the centre-backs and between them; the striker dropping behind the most advanced central midfielder; a full-back overlapping or underlapping its winger (1 s); a full-back stepping inside (18 m or more from the touchline, 5 m ahead of the centre-backs) before the final third. The final-third rate compares possessions with the rotation against those without.
definitions.control: Possession against control. Purposeful possessions reach the final third or a shot; sterile ones string 5 or more completed passes without either. The read compares possession with field tilt: control with territory (both 55% or more), possession without penetration (55% or more of the ball, under 50% of the final-third passes), territory without the ball (45% or less of the ball, 45% or more of the territory), pinned back (both under 45% and 40%), otherwise balanced.
definitions.ppda_intervals: PPDA as in Live analytics (opponent passes in its own 60% ÷ this team's duels and interceptions there), by half and by 15 minutes. High regains are open-play regains in the attacking 40% (x ≥ 60); their shots are within 15 s.
definitions.finishing: Goals minus xG per shooter: above zero, more goals than the chances' quality suggests. One match is far too small a sample to call anyone a good or poor finisher.
definitions.analyst_notes: Each note pairs a number (with its sample) with moments to watch on the replay: the data says what happened, the pictures show why. The notes do not explain causes; they point to where to look.

limitations: Synthetic data: the events and the 5 Hz player positions are generated from fictional tendencies. Off-ball movement between events is illustrative.
Phases, counters and set pieces are classified from the event stream with fixed windows. Real analysts judge where a transition ends by the shape of both teams, not by a timer.

Counter-pressing, blocks, recovery runs, full-back roles and rotations come from synthetic positions, so they show what the generator planted plus noise. Thresholds are documented conventions, not calibrated against real tracking data.

Expected threat is learned from 24 synthetic matches built by the same scripted generator, so it inherits the generator's habits (for example keepers' long balls that reach a forward directly). It is not a model of real football.
Free kicks and throw-ins are rare or absent in the synthetic events (fouls are recorded only as stoppages and the ball goes out mostly for goal kicks), so the set-piece phase is mostly corners.
One match is a small sample. Read rates with their counts, and the analyst notes as prompts for what to watch, not conclusions.
